claude (triage): Q2304 answers that a single suspended Digimon or Tamer counts toward "every 2 of your opponent's suspended Digimon and Tamers", so a mixed pair counts. DCGO agrees: BT13_060.cs:222 counts `IsSuspended && (IsDigimon || IsTamer)` and divides by 2. The YAML for BT13-060 (when_attacking, `trash_top_security` with an any_of Digimon/Tamer suspended count, floor_div 2) implements the same rule. I replayed the exam line sim-only with `exam_probe`. At projection 15, which is before the attack, p1.security is 5. At projection 16, after the attack, p1.security is 3: one card trashed by the clause plus one security check. That equals the DCGO value of 3. So our current engine honours the ruling. The recorded "ours 4" is what you would get if the Tamer were not counted (no trash, one check). I did not confirm this, and it probably came from an engine build that predated the fix_card commit 708a0aa23. The exam's `expect_ruling` asserts `at: 15, p1.security: 3`. Projection 15 is the pre-attack board, so that assertion cannot hold in any engine. The scenario's own comments admit this off-by-one. Fix: change `at: 15` to `at: 16`, the post-attack projection, and re-run the oracle. The ruling's count of 2 holds there.

claude (triage): Q2669 says the trigger activates during the breeding phase, and the main phase comes only after all effects have activated. The exam's `expect_ruling` asserts `at: 11 → phase: main`. I probed our side with `inspect_step: 11`. That is the state before step 11, the `select: {yes: true}` answer to "You may hatch in your breeding area". The hatch prompt is the last part of the Ukkomon (BT16-082) trigger's own resolution. Ours is parked in `SelectEffectChoice` there, a Select* phase that stands for the interrupted Breeding phase. The ruling says the phase must still be breeding at that point, so asserting `main` misreads the answer. The ruling is not violated by our engine. The line also stops right after the hatch answer, so it never reaches the point where main begins. The `at: 9` assert fails for another reason. Our engine is in Select* phases (SelectReveal at 9, SelectPermutation at 10) during selection prompts, and the guide treats `phase` at a selection boundary as representation, not rules state. Fix: drop the `at: 11 phase main` assert. Append a step after the hatch answer, for example the actor's `pass` at `main_phase`, which needs the hatch resolution to finish and so shows main is reached. Then assert `phase: main` at that new later index. Keep a breeding-phase assert only at a non-selection boundary, such as `at: 8` before the move or the state immediately after the move resolves, and do not assert `breeding` at Select* prompts. The line did not run on DCGO's side beyond the mismatch (12 of 12 steps compared, clean), so DCGO and ours agree.

claude (triage): The stop happens in the setup, not in the BT26-050 clause. The line plays ST24-12 on T3 and then expects an `OptionalSkill` prompt so it can decline. That effect reads "By trashing the bottom face-down card from under any of your Tamers, you may return…". In DCGO, `CanActivateCondition` (ST24_12.cs:59-62) needs one of your Tamers to have a face-down source card. The scenario has no Tamer on p0's field, so DCGO never triggers the effect and goes straight to `main_phase`. Our engine does offer an optional prompt there. Both engines still reach the same state, and the clause under test is BT26-050#effect#5, whose Option [Main] has not been reached. The oracle compared only 6 steps and found no divergence before the stop, so it measured nothing about the clause itself. The expectation at that step (`expect: {prompt: OptionalSkill}` after the decline) is a non-discriminating assumption about an unrelated card. Fix for the author: drop the ST24-12 decline step and expect `main_phase` straight after the play. Or better, use a DATA SQUAD enabler whose On Play has no optional prompt. Keep the rest of the line: BT26-050 played as an Option, selecting both opposing Digimon to suspend, then assert the digivolve and unsuspend locks. Separately, our prompt for an unpayable cost on ST24-12 is a possible engine difference, but it does not bear on this clause.

claude (triage): The line, not either engine, is broken. The DCGO job failed with "MultipleSkills: wanted card 'BT26-076' is AMBIGUOUS ... offered 2 times by [BT26-076,BT26-094,BT26-076,BT26-094]. Add select_ordinal". BT26_076.cs:135 registers the reactive digivolve on both OnDiscardHand and OnDigivolutionCardDiscarded. In this line the Tamer-source trash and the P1 hand trash each trigger it, so MultipleSkills lists each skill twice. The step `select: {cards: [BT26-076], dcgo_only: true}` expecting MultipleSkills has no `select_ordinal`, so DCGO stopped there. Everything after that step (OptionalSkill, SelectCardEffect, Keenan declines) is never reached on DCGO's side.

The step-18 memory divergence (ours -5, DCGO -3) is an alignment artifact, not a rules disagreement. The three sim-only rows (trigger order, target, "pay") are placed before actor 1's SelectHandEffect row in the YAML. DCGO has not yet reached the reactive digivolve at that row, so it has not paid the digivolve cost. A sim-only probe of the same prefix, run up to the Tamer selection, shows our engine asks P1's hand trash ("Trash 1 card in your hand") immediately after the Tamer-source trash. So the order matches DCGO: the hand pick comes first, and the reactive trigger resolves after the [When Digivolving] effect finishes. Nothing was shown to differ on timing or optionality.

Fix for the author:
1. Add `select_ordinal` (0 or 1) to the MultipleSkills step (`select: {cards: [BT26-076], dcgo_only: true}`). The candidates are `[0:BT26-076, 1:BT26-094, 2:BT26-076, 3:BT26-094]`, so the ordinal is 0-based among BT26-076's own candidates (0..1).
2. Reorder or re-time the sim-only rows (trigger order, target, "pay") so the memory comparison is made at a point where both engines have paid the same costs. Place them after P1's hand pick, or mark the memory comparison accordingly.
3. Re-run the oracle pass.
